newsitem.title: USA: Foundation, Health in talks - sources.
newsitem.headline: Foundation, Health in talks - sources.

text.p: Foundation Health Corp and Health Systems International, two of the nation's largest health maintenance organizations, are in merger talks, industry sources said Tuesday.
Neither Foundation nor Health Systems would confirm the speculation, but Foundation announced Monday it was having talks concerning a combination with an undisclosed party.

Bankers said Foundation has talked with other companies as its search for a partner intensified with last month's announcement that Pacificare Health Systems would buy FHP International Inc for $2.1 billion.
They said Foundation had also recently approached WellPoint Health Networks Inc, another California managed-care company.
"WellPoint had considered a merger with Foundation, but it wasn't at the right price," said a source familiar with the situation.
On Monday, Foundation said the deal being discussed would result in a nominal value to shareholders below Foundation's September 13 closing price of $36.13.
Analysts said the value of the deal would range from $1.5 billion to $2.0 billion.
Health Systems held merger talks with WellPoint last year, but a deal fell through due to disagreements over titles and responsibilities between those companies' chairmen.
Investment bankers and analysts said this could be a sticking point for Health Systems and Foundation, as well.

Several analysts remained skeptical. "They have two very strong-willed CEOs," said Mary O'Connell, analyst with Josephthal, Lyon and Ross. "There are other alternatives, and discussions are only preliminary. Discussions among companies are quite common," she said.

Other analysts said Health Systems was the likely candidate based on Foundation's statement on Monday which said if the deal proceeds, it would be on a pooling-of-interests, common-stock basis and is expected to be a merger of equals.

"It makes strategic sense for Foundation to merge with Health Systems," said Todd Richter, analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds. "There's only a limited number of organizations that could participate in a pooling transaction due to accounting regulations," he added.
